opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: Tron USDT egress fee inflated ~17x (≈$4 → ≈$72): simulated-swap TRX price accepts a dust-pool fill
opportunities.summary: ## Summary The protocol-level **egress fee for USDT on Tron is currently \~17x too high**: **\~71.61 USDT**, against a real on-chain broadcast cost of **10.7757 TRX (~$3.68)**. The TRX-denominated gas model is fine (\~12.668 TRX vs 10.776 TRX actually burned, +17.6%). The inflation happens entirely in the **TRX → USDT price conversion**, which for TRX is sourced from a rolled-back 20-USDC simulated swap against Chainflip's own TRX/USDC pool. That pool is currently dust, so the probe returns a price of **~$5.65/TRX against a market price of \~$0.3416** — and the only guard on that value is `.filter(|v| *v > 0)`. ## Impact - Users swapping to USDT on Tron are overcharged \~$68 per swap. On the swap below the egress fee was **2.45% of the output**. - Fill-or-kill does not protect against it (see "Secondary finding"). - Tron **ingress** is hit by the same path: `ingress_fees.Tron.USDT` ≈ **63.52 USDT**. - Any asset lacking a Chainlink feed and egressing a non-gas asset is exposed to the same failure mode. ## Reproduction (live, mainnet) ```bash curl -s https://mainnet-archive.chainflip.io -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"cf_environment","param

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
